harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every command (with invoking user, target user, host, cwd, and timestamp) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-commands-log (Defaults logfile=..., Defaults log_year, Defaults !syslog), which suppresses sudo's syslog/authpriv command entries so they no longer appear in the general auth.log. Verified with a real sudo call from a separate test user, confirmed exclusion from auth.log, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol proving persistence: captured pre-restart boot_id/config baseline, issued a native shutdown -r now, polled until node1 reconnected with a new boot_id, and re-verified the sudoers config and correct log routing behavior post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected existing sudo/syslog behavior on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04) and confirmed sudo commands were being logged to /var/log/auth.log via syslog by default
Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-commands-log with Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", Defaults log_year, Defaults !syslog
Validated syntax with visudo -cf, set file permissions (0440 on sudoers snippet, 0600 on log file)

Created a temporary test user (sudologtest) with a NOPASSWD sudo rule, ran a sudo command as that user, confirmed it appeared in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp and did NOT appear in /var/log/auth.log, then cleaned up the test user and temporary sudoers rule
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, sudoers config content, and log line count on node1
Issued a native shutdown -r now reboot on node1 with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirming a new boot_id and near-zero uptime, proving an actual restart

Post-reboot, re-verified the sudoers snippet persisted, /var/log/sudo-commands.log persisted and continued accumulating new entries, and confirmed post-reboot sudo commands still excluded from auth.log

evidence.requirement: sudo commands are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: Created and validated /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-commands-log with Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log; log file shows timestamped entries with user and command for each sudo invocation

evidence.requirement: entries kept out of the general system log (auth.log/syslog)
evidence.summary: Test user sudologtest ran a sudo command; entry appeared in sudo-commands.log with user=sudologtest, and grep for that user/command in auth.log returned 0 matches, confirming syslog suppression via Defaults !syslog
Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45, uptime, sudoers config content, and 49-line log file count before reboot
Issued sudo shutdown -r now via backgrounded nohup; command returned exit 0 before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: changed boot identity proves actual restart
evidence.summary: Node briefly unreachable (connection timed out) then returned with boot_id 3e90fb02-9cc0-4fef-a228-13a3153406aa (different from baseline) and uptime 4.02s

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and correct log routing
evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers snippet intact, sudo-commands.log continued growing with new timestamped entries, and grep of auth.log COMMAND= lines showed only pre-fix entries (hostname still 'ubuntu24', all timestamps <=11:17:18) with zero new command entries post-reboot
